Subject: Security addons pricing — pilot pricing scenario and scale path

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together two concrete pricing pathways for the security/compliance add-ons you asked about (audit logs retention, KMS/HSM, residency). I attached a rough pilot SOW and a simple pricing model to make this easier to evaluate.

High level options for a 3–6 month pilot: 
- Pilot A (Lean): No dedicated HSM seat during pilot, use shared KMS proxy (per-request HSM offload). Audit logs retained at 90 days (compressed storage). Price: $28k/month for expected token volume during pilot. Implementation fee: $12k one-time.
- Pilot B (Full-Spec): Dedicated HSM seat with HSM-backed keys, audit logs 13 months retained on hot-tier for first 3 months then archived. Price: $42k/month. Implementation fee: $6k one-time (we amortize some bootstrapping). First 3 months HSM seat discounted 50% as a pilot credit.

Other levers we can use to meet procurement constraints: 6-month committed credit, convert pilot credits into first-year commit, or amortize HSM seat as a one-time implementation fee and lower monthly recurring. I spelled those options out in the attached spreadsheet.

Quick asks so we can finalize numbers:
1) Approx. expected sustained QPS and peak QPS during pilot (this affects batching assumptions).
2) Audit log retention target (90 / 180 / 395 days?).
3) Whether Medtrax requires logs to be resident in a single geography for the pilot.

If Helpful: I can put together a short two-column pricing exhibit (pilot vs scale) showing the convert path from pilot credits to annual commitment with estimated unit economics.

Next steps: Would you like me to send a formal SOW + DocuSign with Pilot A and Pilot B options, or would you prefer we iterate on a single recommended path?

Attachments: pilot_SOW_draft.pdf (PDF), pilot_pricing_model.xlsx (XLSX)

Cheers,
Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Appreciate the rapid follow-up and the two-path framing. A few constraints from our side:
- Our pilot budget envelope is roughly $80k total (OPEX) — we generally avoid large up-front CAPEX for pilots.
- Procurement wants a line-item split: implementation vs recurring so we can approve monthly spend.
- Audit retention: target initially 180 days; if we see low retrieval rates we can archive to cold after month 3.
- Residency: logs must remain in US for this pilot; long-term we may need EU as well but not for this stage.

Question on HSM: do you have an option to provide HSM-backed keys but priced as a per-request usage charge instead of a fixed seat for pilot? That's our preferred model if available.

I attached the trimmed security questionnaire you asked for — mostly for alignment on data flows.

If you can get Pilot A down to $24k/month by amortizing more of the implementation work into a one-time fee, that would get us closer. Otherwise Pilot B will probably blow the pilot budget even with the 50% seat discount.

Hi Samir / Jordan —

Quick implementation notes from the solutions side to align the pricing assumptions: 
- 180d retention (US) is straightforward. Cheapest option that meets audit-readiness is: store logs hot for 45 days, then compressed cold-tier for 135 days. Retrieval SLA on cold-tier is <24 hours which works for most audit scenarios.
- Per-request HSM bridging: technically we implement a lightweight KMS proxy that signs outbound keys to HSM when required. That path avoids provisioning a dedicated HSM VM for the pilot and is the lowest friction option.
- If Medtrax expects bursts that exceed our continuous batching assumptions (e.g., 10x peaks for short windows), we'll need to size burst capacity separately — that can be added as a capped burst allowance on the SOW.

Proposal to keep the pilot within your $80k envelope:
1) Lean Pilot (recommended): $16k one-time implementation + $24k/month recurring (includes per-request HSM estimated at $6.5k/month based on 12k calls/day). Total for 3-month pilot = $88.5k.
2) Concession: Redwood will provide a $8.5k pilot credit applied to the first invoice if you sign within 10 business days. That brings the 3-month on-paper spend to ~$80k.

If Procurement prefers no credits and a clean split for accounting, we can convert that $8.5k concession into a one-time implementation fee reduction instead. Either way we can make the numbers procurement-friendly.

Next step: If Samir approves the lean pilot + credit, Jordan — please send the SOW with the two-line exhibit (Impl fee + Recurring) and include the DocuSign link. I'll attach an implementation timeline (sprint-level) to the SOW showing workstreams and acceptance criteria.
